summary: Sokichi Tsuda (1873–1961) was a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and sinology who studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō (~1890–1891). He held posts at the SMR Research Department, University of Tokyo, and Waseda University, which he founded in 1935.
Sokuo Eto (1888–1958) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. He founded Dokenryo in 1937 and served as a professor at Komazawa University in 1953.

Solomon George FitzHerbert is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford, where he was a Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies, and held a research post at the CNRS (attested 2019).

Soma Thera (1898–1960) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, and under traditional teacher Jetavana Sayadaw (1936). He was a member of the Servants of the Buddha around 1926.

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held positions at the French Institute of Pondicherry, Columbia University as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit, and Kyoto University as Professor in 2011.
Somboon Watana works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Panjab University in 1999, where he studied under doctoral supervisors Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma.

Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara (1913–2013) studied at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara and under Swami Satyananda Puri and Vajirayanavangsa. In Buddhist and religious studies, he served as Director at Mahamakut Buddhist University, meditation teacher at Kasetsart University, and abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara.

Somphong Santacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, studying under MA supervisor Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

Sonam Chhoki is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D at SOAS University of London. She has held a post as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Gyatso (born 1933) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a research assistant at the Toyo Bunko (~1960–1968) and as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

Sonam Kachru is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold. He has held appointments at the University of Chicago Divinity School, Forum Transregionale Studien, and MPIWG.

Sonam Thakchoe is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1999–2002) under mentors Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, later taking a post there around 2005.

Sonam Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his doctoral studies under Gray Tuttle and also studied under teachers including Namgyel Khenzur Dawa, Drepung Khenzur Gyatso, Samdhong Rinpoche, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Lobsang Trinley.

Songeun Choe is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and completed a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

Sonja Arntzen (born 1945) is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1970–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, and also studied with Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

Sonja Glauch (born 1967) studied linguistics at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, completing her Magisterexamen, Promotion, and Habilitation. Her posts include Heidelberg University Library, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, a guest professorship at the University of Vienna, and a professorship replacement at the University of Munich.

Sonya S. Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology who earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Wu Hung. She taught at Swarthmore College and held posts at Stanford University and the University of Southern California.

Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University under Seung-won Seo, completed a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, and holds a post at Dongguk University.

Sophus Bugge (1833–1907) was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1858. He held posts at Uppsala University and at the University of Oslo, where he became professor of comparative philology, comparative Indo-European linguistics, and Old Norse in 1866.

Soshuku Shibatani (born 1954) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Waseda University and Koyasan University. He has held positions at Sonoda Women's University, Junrei Henro Kenkyukai (2014), and Koyasan University (attested 2015).
